standard_prerequisites.name: Kingman subadditive ergodic theorem, Egorov theorem and Birkhoff/Poincare recurrence
standard_prerequisites.statement: Use the author-cited standard ergodic inputs. Quantitative recurrence Lemma5.1 is stated in full in450-454, with author reference Bochi Lemma3.12. No recursive prerequisite proof collection.

core_obligations: Handle the negative-infinite Lyapunov exponent case as the author does
Use an Egorov-uniform positive-measure set and quantitative return times to construct N long ordered cocycle blocks
Apply the fixed n=N order-preserving spectral-radius inequality, preserving all products in their author order
Compare uniform growth errors over returned blocks and derive the a.e. spectral-radius growth equality
items.difficulty_reason: H2: the own ergodic argument converts a purported spectral-growth gap on a positive-measure set into N well-separated return blocks inside an Egorov-uniform set. The quantitative recurrence scale must be matched to the fixed-length algebraic inequality, and its multiplicative errors controlled relative to a selected contiguous block. This is a nonroutine recurrence/uniformisation argument beyond merely quoting Kingman or the matrix inequality; the full author core450-507 is counted. The substantial algebraic inequality remains explicitly linked to existing1920 rather than counted again as a new lemma.

Actual theorem is nonlinear order-preserving homogeneous cone spectral-radius duality via monotone prenorm infimum, not a.e. spectral/norm growth equality for one integrable linear cocycle.
